papers.title: Dynamics of collective creativity in AI art competitions
papers.abstract: Abstract Creativity is a fundamental part of cultural evolution, but the mechanisms by which groups produce novelty are notoriously difficult to infer from the historical record. Iterated learning experiments have shown that cultural transmission reliably distorts artifacts toward the inductive biases of learners, but most of this work uses linear chains of human participants, and it is unclear how these dynamics play out in the networked, human-AI systems that increasingly shape cultural production. papers.title: Surveillance Path Dependence: Technological and Institutional Lock-In of Digital Surveillance Infrastructures in China
papers.abstract: Digital surveillance infrastructures are widely critiqued for their use-side problems of access, privacy, and discrimination, but meaningful intervention requires understanding how these infrastructures are developed and stabilized in the first place. This paper examines China’s health code systems (HCSs) as a revelatory case of path dependence in the development of digital surveillance infrastructures. papers.tldr_zh: 以中国健康码系统为案例，通过新闻、访谈与田野调查追踪数字监控基础设施如何嵌入支付宝和微信生态并形成技术与制度锁定。

papers.title: Developmental asymmetries in equilibrium selection
papers.abstract: Abstract Coordination problems are central to social and economic life and often involve multiple equilibria. Classical theories identify two canonical principles for equilibrium selection: maximizing payoffs and minimizing strategic risk. These principles differ in what they demand of a decision-maker: payoff-based coordination can be reached by recognizing that one equilibrium pays more, whereas risk-based coordination requires reasoning about what happens when coordination fails. papers.tldr_zh: 用2000余名10-20岁被试玩两个协调博弈并陈述理由，发现均衡选择中收益原则与风险原则的使用随年龄发展呈不对称变化。

papers.title: The Community Archive: An Ethically Sourced X (Twitter) Dataset
papers.abstract: We present The Community Archive, a novel dataset of over 5 million posts from the social media site X (previously known as Twitter). In contrast with other large scale social media datasets, which are generally assembled without user consent via web scrapers, The Community Archive uses an opt-in model to obtain author consent for every post in the dataset. This enables us to release both the metadata and the content of users' posts at a previously unprecedented scale. Our dataset supports work in a wide variety of domains, including social network analysis, narrative tracking, and diachronic
papers.tldr_zh: 发布500万条经用户明示同意采集的X帖子数据集，含元数据与正文，并示例分析内容同质性。

papers.title: Network topology shapes consensus and vulnerability in LLM populations
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are deployed in interacting populations, their collective behaviour depends not only on the models but also on who interacts with whom. Studies of convention formation in LLM populations have mainly tested well-mixed interactions. We place policies extracted from four LLMs on fully connected, random regular, and heterogeneous networks, with $10^3$ to $10^5$ agents playing the naming game. papers.tldr_zh: 将四个LLM策略置于不同网络拓扑中玩命名博弈，发现拓扑影响共识速度、是否达成及对对抗的脆弱性。

papers.title: A phase transition for the strength of weak ties
papers.abstract: Abstract Granovetter's ``strength of weak ties'' argument links local triadic closure to the global importance of weak relationships, but it does not by itself quantify when strong ties can or cannot sustain large-scale connectivity. We study the subgraph formed by strong ties under a uniform, edgewise closure condition. A strong-tie graph is called p-transitive when, for every ordered adjacent pair (A,B), at least a fraction p of the strong neighbors of B other than A are also strong neighbors of A. papers.title: Core-periphery structure induces double phase transitions in information cascades
papers.abstract: Double phase transitions in spreading processes are commonly associated with additional dynamical or structural complexity. Here, we show that such transitions can emerge naturally in prevalent networks exhibiting a core-periphery (CP) organization. Specifically, we consider threshold-driven spreading on CP networks constructed from the stochastic block model, which is characterized by three parameters: the relative core size $r$, the CP coupling strength $μ$, and the fraction of intra-block link allocation $α$. papers.title: Causal asymmetry suggests productivity underlies scientific collaboration
papers.abstract: Abstract Scientific productivity and collaboration are closely related, yet the causal direction between these two dimensions of academic careers remains unclear. Here we analyze the careers of 26,876 Brazilian researchers holding a nationally prestigious fellowship across multiple disciplines to test whether productivity shapes collaboration or the reverse. papers.tldr_zh: 用因果发现框架分析2.7万巴西学者，发现生产力驱动合作而非相反。

papers.title: From lifestyle to citizenship: Social influence and political consumerism in egocentric networks
papers.abstract: Political consumerism has become a widespread form of civic engagement, yet the social mechanisms driving boycotting and buycotting remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates how perceived citizenship norms within individuals’ egocentric networks are associated with their own civic orientations and subsequent participation in consumer activism. Using a national survey of 543 U.S. adults reporting on 1822 social ties, we integrate social learning and social influence theories to examine how network environments cultivate engaged and dutiful citizenship norms. papers.title: X-pressing Intimacy: Mental Health Disclosure After Twitter Acquisition
papers.abstract: Social media platforms provide spaces for individuals to disclose mental health experiences and seek support, yet how these disclosures evolve during major shifts in platform governance remains unclear. We examine mental health self-disclosure surrounding Elon Musk's October 2022 acquisition of Twitter, analyzing approximately 824K tweets across anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder (BD), borderline personality disorder (BPD), and suicidal ideation (SI) or related experiences, alongside 266K comparison tweets. papers.title: Condensation and optimal targeting of repeated forcing in heterogeneous networks
papers.abstract: Many networks receive repeated external forcing through a subset of entry nodes, for example infections imported from another population, information seeded by a campaign, or invasive species arriving through ports. We study how concentrating such forcing on important entry nodes, with seeding probability $π_i\propto w_i^γ$, changes the size of the resulting cascades in a stochastic SIR model on bipartite networks. papers.title: Geospatial Dynamics of Online Attention to Nuclear Power in Japan Before and After Fukushima
papers.abstract: Nuclear power is increasingly seen as necessary for sustainable development, but this role depends on informed public engagement and support. Building this support requires understanding what citizens want to know, as reflected in their spontaneous online searches. To map this demand, we present the first long-term (2004-2024), prefecture-level analysis of Google Trends data on nuclear power in Japan. papers.title: From friction to alignment: Algorithmic imaginaries and the Trump autocomplete controversy on Reddit
papers.abstract: Employing topic modelling, this study analyses a collection of 157 submissions and 10,032 comments from Reddit surrounding users’ perceptions of censorship and bias by Google's autocomplete function following the Trump assassination attempt in July 2024. The discussions are examined through the framing of ‘friction of relevance’, operationalised as the tension between the expectations of individual users and algorithmic moderation by search engines, the strategies users employ to navigate it, and the outcomes when the friction is not resolved.
